LESSON: WRITING 8.4.1 SPELLING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.4: Writing 8.4.1 Spelling
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 8.4.1 Spelling, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we spell words correctly? 2. How can we write legibly and neatly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 8.4.1 Spelling together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and Imagination: The learner makes decisions as they make words related to parts of the body from jumbled letters and fingerspell them.

Values:
Responsibility: hard work is enhanced as the learner engages in assigned roles and duties in their groups.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Effective communication is enhanced as learners fingerspell words correctly.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learners are able to relate the knowledge of spelling to spell words correctly in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Manual alphabet chart, flash cards, internet, posters, online dictionaries, assistive devices fitted with appropriate technologies such as hearing aids and

amplifiers, adapted course books, flash cards, sign language dictionary, internet, signed audio-visual recordings
